one_line_summary: Honda power-assist trolley with two rear driven omnidirectional wheels and two front casters, in which handle force sets provisional target longitudinal/lateral speeds (or a velocity vector) that are scaled by a common correction coefficient when an upper limit is exceeded, preserving travel direction.

E1.quote: a pair of omnidirectional wheels 3 are provided at the lower portion of the rear portion 2A of the vehicle body 2 . Left and right casters 13 are supported at the lower portion of the front portion 2B
E1.note: Four-wheeled trolley (2 rear omni wheels + 2 front casters) carrying devices such as an X-ray scanner; heavy-load/hospital-bed context not stated explicitly.

E2.quote: each omnidirectional wheel 3 includes a frame 17, a pair of drive discs 18 rotatably supported by the frame 17, and an annular main wheel 19 disposed between the pair of drive discs 18.
E2.note: Two of four wheels are active, but they are drive-disk omnidirectional wheels, not steer-and-drive wheels with a 360 deg steering drive.

E3.quote: Each caster 13 has a fork 13A rotatably coupled to the arm 14 about an axis extending vertically
E3.note: Passive wheels are swivel casters (front), but the two active wheels are a left/right pair on the rear, not diagonal.

E4.quote: The handle 5 is supported by the handle holder 35 via the force sensor 6
E4.note: Push handle on a three-axis force sensor.

E5.quote: the control device 7 sets the target speed vector provisional value vtp of the vehicle body 2 based on the load detected by the force sensor 6
E5.note: Handle force is turned into a target velocity vector (with speed limiting that preserves direction), but a target angular velocity from the moment is also commanded in the embodiment, and the mapping is given as e.g. a proportional gain on force (vtp1 = k1*fs1), not dependent on measured instantaneous speed/acceleration.

E6.quote: The control device 7 sets the respective target rotation speeds rt of the electric motors 25 based on the target longitudinal speed vt1, the target lateral speed vt2, and the target angular speed ωt.
E6.note: Vector converted into per-motor speeds of the omni-wheel drive disks; no per-wheel steering angle.

combination_note: E2+E3 not disclosed: two driven wheels plus two swivel casters, but the driven wheels are omnidirectional wheels side by side at the rear, not diagonal swerve modules. E5->E6 partial: handle force -> target velocity vector (claim 9) -> per-motor rotation speeds, but with no steering angle per wheel and no speed/acceleration-aware interpretation; rotation is also commanded. Closest overlap is claim 9's force-to-velocity-vector concept; biggest gap is the wheel type/layout.
